The Governor of Gujarat, H.E. Sundersinh Bhandari, inaugurated the ‘Pramukh Swami Computer Institute’ in the hostel campus. The introduction of a post-graduate diploma in computer application, recognised by the Sardar Patel University, is a new step in the Sanstha’s effort in promoting computer education. The Governor appreciated the socio-spiritual activities of the Sanstha. In his blessings Swamishri emphasised the importance of dharma in life.
At 10.52 a.m. Swamishri flew from Gandhidham and reached Vadodara at 11.49 a.m. After meeting the sadhus and devotees Swamishri left Vadodara at 12.00 noon and reached Vidyanagar at 12.55 p.m.

At 5.35 p.m. Sundersinh Bhandari, arrived for the inauguration ceremony of ‘Pramukh Swami Computer Institute’ at the hostel campus. The computer institute will be offering a course in postgraduate diploma in computer application. It is recognised by the Sardar Patel University of Vidyanagar. The inauguration ceremony took place amidst Vedic rites at the hands of the Governor. Swamishri and the Governor made a short tour and saw the 27 new computers installed in the institute.

In the assembly that followed, various dignitaries and officials honored Swamishri and the Governor. First, the Vice-Chancellor of ‘Sardar Patel University’ addressed the assembly. The Governor, Shri Sundersinh Bhandari, lauded the efforts of the Sanstha, "The progress of science in a spiritual environment will surely be the gift of India to the world. We find science is progressing tremendously but the dimension of discrimination is missing. Instead of creating we are declining towards destruction. And the reason for this tendency is lack of dharma...

" In his blessings, Swamishri said, "Science has given momentum but it lacks dharma. Man is merely running blindly. He fails to think that whatever he is doing, will it be useful? Will it help the country, society or religion? He is blindly running after money, earning a quick buck through pedaling drugs, regardless of whether the person dies or destroys himself. "It is heartening that science is progressing. It has given us many gifts, but due to lack of dharma man has become immoral, sinful and adulterous. That is why science needs dharma. Our great sages have been saying from antiquity that life without dharma is similar to that of an animal.
"God is the greatest scientist. We have computers, made by man and the maker of man is God. When we forget God and misuse science because of our ego then the consequences are pain and misery..."

From 4.44 pm to 5.44 pm a solar eclipse was observed by Swamishri, sadhus and devotees by doing bhajan and listening to discourses. At the conclusion of the assembly Swamishri blessed the gathering, “Every person prays to God when he experiences pain and misery in life. He goes to the mandir and engages himself in doing bhajan and mala. When a farmer reaps a good harvest of peanuts or cotton he gets a hefty sum. Then he gets a beautiful cart, decorating it with rupee coins. But he does not think that his wealth was attained by God’s grace and that he should please Him. As one gets more and more wealth one tends to forget God…”
Keys to Academic Success

On 16 March 2006 at Sarangpur, Swamishri wrote his blessings for the annual diary of the BAPS School in Selvas. He gave a lucid guideline for success for all students, “Every student should pay attention while studying in class, have concentration, do one’s homework regularly, repeat whatever one has learnt everyday and respect one’s teachers and parents. Then Bhagwan Swaminarayan will bless you with success.”
Over Coming Lust

On 19 March 2006 in Sarangpur, a youth revealed his problem, “How can I overcome lust?” Swamishri blessed him and replied, “Always pray to God, strive to observe moral rules and do not watch bad things on TV. Also do not look at (enticing) posters and magazines. If you look at obscene pictures then your mind will think accordingly.”
Self-Fault

Another youth candidly expressed to Swamishri, “For the last one year I have been plagued with the question as to whether Satsang is right or wrong? Because of this I have lapsed in my morals and have started drinking liquor.” Swamishri replied, “There is nothing wrong with Satsang. There is no fault in it. The fault lies in the individual. It is because of one’s mundane desires that such thoughts arise. So, you should pray and do bhajan. Maharaj will shower his compassion upon you.”
Eradicating Cynical Thinking

On 26 March 2006 in Sarangpur, Yagnesh Patel asked Swamishri, “We may not speak ill of someone but what should we do when we get cynical thoughts in our minds? How can we overcome them?” Swamishri guided, “Do bhajan. And whenever such critical or cynical conversations take place then leave at once. When such thoughts arise in one’s mind then engage oneself in God’s bhakti or some other good activity.”
Confidence Boosting

On 30 March 2006 in Sarangpur, an aspirant came with his son. He wished that his son be blessed for intelligence by Swamishri. The father explained, “An astrologer stated that my son does not have any intelligence. Ever since then he has been lagging behind in his studies.” Swamishri interrupted and assured the boy, “He does not have less intelligence. Chant the name of Swaminarayan and pray daily. Worship God and make efforts in your studies. Have faith and resolve in your mind that you want to achieve 80% or 90% and you will get good marks.” Swamishri infused confidence in the boy’s mind.

The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.

During a phone conversation about the murti-pratishtha of the shikharbaddh mandir at Limbdi, Santswarup Swami said, "You said that you would come to Limbdi and stay there. So when you come to Limbdi, please stay, and do not even mention leaving."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj immediately said, "We do not stay bound by anyone."

ds.t: We are not bound by anyone

st.t: Earth Hour Celebration at Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi joined the international community in participating in the world’s biggest environmental event – The Earth Hour – on 29 March 2014 from 8:30 pm to 9:30 pm . For one hour, Swaminarayan Akshardham supported its continual commitment for environmental conservation by switching off its lights. In its fifth year of participation, Swaminarayan Akshardham continues to support environmental projects that promote the awareness and education of a cleaner and safer planet. Around the world, Earth Hour is embraced by the global community, transcending race, culture, age and economics as individuals take leadership in their communities in the pursuit of a cleaner and safer planet. The purpose of celebrating ‘The Earth Hour’ is to save electrical power, and to take a stand against climate change. The purpose was to stop the degradation of the earth’s natural environment and build a future where people live in harmony by reducing light pollution and the carbon footprint. Across the world, other famous landmarks that dimmed their lights to join in the celebration of the Earth Hour included the Eiffel Tower in Paris, Houses of the British Parliament, Buckingham Palace, Tower Bridge and the London Eye in Britain, the Empire State Building in New York, the Kremlin and Red Square in Moscow, Burj Khalifa in Dubai, the Bosphorus Bridge in Turkey and the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin.
After Mahant Swami Maharaj's puja was complete, the trustees came together at the end and garlanded him.
The trustees asked: "Swami! Is there any message for us trustees?"
With a gesture of his hand, Swamishri said: "Samp (unity and harmony)."
2 days earlier, in a skit, Swamishri had given the same message to the children who played the roles of trustees. Whether a child or an elder, this is Swamishri's lasting message.
On the flight from Lenasia to Dar es Salaam:

A light conversation was going on between the sadhus and Mahant Swami Maharaj. Just then Atmaswarupdas Swami related: "2 days ago Swamishri told me: 'Why should we rest? Meeting the devotees is itself our rest.'"
It is everyone's experience that we never feel tired or bored meeting someone we love.
"Meeting the devotees is itself our rest": this sentence shows Swamishri's love and closeness towards the devotees.
